summary:
**NINO – Smart Astronaut Health Support System**

NINO is a proposed integrated healthcare solution designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions and address health challenges associated with microgravity.

The project introduces a smart wearable suit that uses mechanical fibers to apply controlled, distributed pressure across the body, with greater support around the lower limbs. This pressure-based concept aims to help manage fluid redistribution and provide additional mechanical support to muscles and bones in microgravity environments.

The proposed hardware system includes pressure sensors, mechanical fibers, and an ESP32 microcontroller to monitor and regulate pressure levels. An additional radiation sensor is designed to monitor environmental radiation exposure.

NINO also includes a digital health monitoring dashboard that displays key health indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, body temperature, stress, and sleep quality, helping astronauts track their health throughout missions.

By combining wearable technology, environmental monitoring, and digital health insights, NINO explores an integrated approach to astronaut healthcare, supporting safer and more sustainable long-duration space exploration.

The website currently demonstrates the interface using simulated data, while full hardware integration and physical testing are planned for future development.
details:
NINO – Smart Astronaut Health Support System

NINO is an integrated astronaut healthcare concept designed to address the physiological challenges of long-duration space missions.

The system combines a smart wearable suit with a digital health monitoring platform. The suit is designed with mechanical fibers that apply controlled, distributed pressure across the body, with greater support around the lower limbs. This pressure-gradient concept aims to explore ways to manage fluid redistribution and provide additional mechanical support in microgravity.

The proposed hardware architecture includes pressure sensors, an ESP32 microcontroller, mechanical fibers, and a radiation sensor. These components are intended to support pressure monitoring and environmental radiation awareness.

The digital platform provides a centralized dashboard for monitoring health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, body temperature, stress, and sleep quality.

The project combines wearable engineering, embedded systems, and web-based health visualization in one concept. Its creative approach is the integration of mechanical support and continuous health monitoring rather than treating them as separate solutions.

The current website demonstrates the interface using simulated data. Full hardware integration, calibration, and physical testing are planned future development stages.
